newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil Range has directors look at Faro.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range has directors look at Faro.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp said on Friday it established a committee of independent directors to review the shutdown of its Faro zinc and lead mine in the Yukon.
Anvil said the committee would comprise Norman Anderson, Robert Korthals, Patrick Mars and Peter Puccetti.

The directors hired independent mining consultants to review the circumstances leading to the shutdown of Faro and examine mine and mill operations and the conditions that could lead to re-opening the mine.
"The board really wanted a technical review," company spokesman Victor Wells said in an interview. "The independence issue was very important."
The company surprised investors earlier this month when it said low zinc and lead prices, poor ore grade and a stronger Canadian dollar would force it to stop mining operations on December 20.
The news sent the company's stock to 1.47 from 6. The stock was at 1.65 today.

Analysts said the independent committee was partly a move to placate angry shareholders. Investors became upset not just with the shutdown but at news that chief executive Kurt Forgaard sold 26,680 shares in early October for more than C$175,000 at prices between C$6.50 and C$6.70 a share.
Forgaard has said he did not know how tenuous the conditions were at the mine until a few days before announcing the shutdown.

"There is a great deal of unhappiness among their shareholders, so I'm sure this (independent committee) is an effort to communicate better," said mining analyst Manford Mallory with Research Capital in Toronto.
He said Anvil Range had lost much of the trust it had built up with shareholders.
